articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Code, Video, and Audio
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 Turbo, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning that can simultaneously process and cross-reference video, audio, and code inputs in a single context window. Benchmarks show a 40% improvement over GPT-5 on complex agentic coding tasks and real-time video understanding. The model also introduces a new structured tool-use protocol that significantly reduces hallucination in multi-step agent workflows.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Graduate-Level Scientific Reasoning
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2, which surpasses previous frontier models on the GPQA Diamond and new SciArena benchmarks designed to test PhD-level reasoning in physics, biology, and mathematics. The model leverages a new mixture-of-experts architecture with over 50 specialized expert modules. Google is integrating Ultra 2 into its research tools across Google Cloud and Google Labs, positioning it as a scientific co-pilot.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude's 'Extended Thinking Chains' for Multi-Hour Autonomous Research Tasks
articles.summary: Anthropic unveiled an update to its Claude model family enabling persistent, multi-hour extended thinking chains that allow the model to autonomously conduct research, synthesize literature, and produce structured reports with minimal human supervision. The system includes built-in self-verification checkpoints and citation auditing. Early enterprise adopters in pharma and legal report significant reductions in analyst workload for due diligence tasks.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in BMW and Amazon Warehouses
articles.summary: Tesla's third-generation Optimus humanoid robot has entered limited commercial deployment at BMW manufacturing facilities in South Carolina and Amazon fulfillment centers in Texas. The Gen 3 units feature improved dexterous manipulation with 22-DOF hands and can autonomously navigate dynamic warehouse environments using onboard vision transformers. Tesla reports the robots are handling bin-picking and parts-kitting tasks at roughly 70% of human worker throughput.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Partners with Microsoft to Deploy Foundation-Model-Powered Humanoids in Data Centers
articles.summary: Figure announced a strategic partnership with Microsoft to deploy its Figure 03 humanoid robots in Azure data centers for hardware maintenance tasks including cable management, drive replacement, and thermal system inspection. The robots run a jointly developed foundation model for physical reasoning that allows zero-shot generalization to new server rack configurations. The partnership signals growing industry confidence that humanoid form factors can address labor shortages in critical infrastructure.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm A14 Process Node Ahead of Schedule
articles.summary: TSMC announced it has commenced volume production on its A14 (1.4nm-class) process node, roughly one quarter ahead of its original roadmap. The node uses gate-all-around nanosheet transistors and backside power delivery, yielding an estimated 20% performance gain and 30% power reduction over the N2 node. Apple, Nvidia, and Qualcomm are confirmed first customers, with chips expected in consumer devices by early 2027.

articles.title: Meta Releases Llama 4 Under Open Weights with Unprecedented 1M-Token Native Context
articles.summary: Meta released Llama 4, its latest open-weights large language model, featuring a native context window of one million tokens without quality degradation. The model uses a novel ring attention variant combined with sparse retrieval heads that maintain coherence over ultra-long documents. Available under a permissive license for both research and commercial use, it is expected to accelerate open-source agentic application development significantly.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance for Second-Generation Brain-Computer Interface with Bidirectional Stimulation
articles.summary: The FDA granted clearance for Neuralink's N2 implant, a second-generation brain-computer interface that supports both high-bandwidth neural recording (over 16,000 channels) and targeted microstimulation for sensory feedback. Clinical trial data showed paralyzed participants achieving cursor control speeds approaching able-bodied baselines and reporting rudimentary tactile sensations through the stimulation pathways. The approval covers a 50-patient expansion trial focused on motor restoration and communication.
